items.story: ZEUS trial: ziltivekimab (Novo Nordisk, interleukin-6 antibody) did not cut heart events in 6,376 people; presented at the American Heart Association meeting and published in NEJM, 2026-11-07
items.note: All figures match the HCPLive report: 3,184 vs 3,192, median 33 months, 561 vs 565 events (17.6% vs 17.7%), hazard ratio 0.99 (0.88-1.11), infection deaths 3.2% vs 2.5%, serious blood clots 1.6% vs 0.6%, low platelets 7.4% vs 3.2%.

items.story: SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT: survodutide (Boehringer Ingelheim / Zealand) did not raise major heart events against placebo, no proven reduction; American Heart Association meeting and The Lancet, 2026-11-09
items.note: Healio gives 5,508 people, matching the claim (the company release gives 5,530). Hazard ratio 0.84 (0.60-1.18) for the three-part outcome; not designed to show a reduction. 'Clears the way for filings' and the comparison with semaglutide are the reader's interpretation, not checked in the source.

items.story: Jaiswal and colleagues, American Journal of Cardiovascular Drugs, 2026-11-07: pooled analysis of nine trials (2,005 people) of colchicine around heart surgery
items.note: Abstract confirms: irregular rhythm after surgery risk ratio 0.70 (0.59-0.83); deaths and strokes no different. Crossref also gives online date 2026-11-07. A pooled analysis about surgery, only loosely tied to preventing heart attacks.

items.story: ZEUS trial of ziltivekimab, neutral result: Mass General Brigham release on EurekAlert, 2026-11-07
items.note: Release confirms late-breaking presentation, simultaneous NEJM paper (DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2612126), Ridker calling colchicine underused in stable disease and pointing upstream (NLRP3 inhibitors). The summary I received did not show the exact phrases 'not statistically significant' or 'this drug in this setting did not work'; the release does say event rates were not reduced.

items.story: Registry NCT04916470 (Novo Nordisk, semaglutide in heart failure with obesity and type 2 diabetes, 617 people): results first posted 2026-11-02
items.note: Registry confirms results first posted 2026-11-02, trial completed 2023-10-11. That it was already published is not checked here but is consistent with a 2023 completion; no new finding.

items.story: Meyer, perspective in the journal Function, 2026-11-03: aged immune cells in thigh muscle after knee ligament tears in mice
items.note: Crossref record with abstract confirms: one author, commentary on mouse work, cites clearing aged cells as helping muscle and cartilage. No trial.

items.story: Registry NCT06263244 (Amsterdam university hospital, 40-person ziltivekimab inflammation study) marked completed, updated 2026-11-06
items.note: Confirmed: completed, main completion 2026-10-30, last update posted 2026-11-06, 40 people, no results posted. I did not check that it is an imaging trial or placebo-controlled.

items.story: Yang and colleagues, BMC Medicine, 2026-11-03: cohort study of colchicine use and heart events in Chinese adults starting urate-lowering treatment
items.note: Title, journal and date confirmed in Crossref. The claim gives no finding and I saw no abstract either, so the direction of the result is unknown. A records study, not a trial.

items.story: ZEUS trial of ziltivekimab, neutral result: Healio report of the American Heart Association session, 2026-11-07
items.note: Figures match: 6,376 people, inflammation marker down 64%, 17.6% vs 17.7%, hazard ratio 0.99 (0.88-1.11), P = 0.84, serious infections 20.4% vs 17.9%, meeting 2026-11-06 to 11-09, HERMES and ARTEMIS described as continuing, patients about ten years older than in the canakinumab trial. Healio's 'HERMES continuing' sits oddly with Novo's own report of 2026-11-04 (item S1012), which says HERMES missed its main goal. The 'colchicine underused' remark is in the hospital release rather than plainly in Healio.

items.story: Novo Nordisk nine-month report, 2026-11-04: 4.6 billion kroner write-down on ziltivekimab; ZEUS and HERMES missed their main goals; ziltivekimab work closed
items.note: Filed copy confirms the 4.6 billion kroner (4,648 million) impairment, the sentence that ZEUS and HERMES did not meet the primary endpoint, and a 'one-time cost related to the ziltivekimab closure'. The statement that HERMES was stopped in September after an interim look is not in the part of the report I could read; not checked.

items.story: Tah and Cheshire, medRxiv preprint, 2026-11-06: records study of GLP-1 drugs added to statins in people with artery disease, 119,911 matched pairs
items.note: Abstract confirms 119,911 pairs, deaths 4.0% vs 7.5% over three years. Not peer reviewed, not a trial. I did not confirm that the group was limited to obese people (the title says artery disease; a subgroup is body mass index 35 and over).

items.story: Registry NCT07920133 first posted 2026-11-05: TARGET-CHD, Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, 1,768 people, colchicine guided by an inflammation blood marker after stenting
items.note: All details confirmed: first posted 2026-11-05, not yet recruiting, start 2026-12-01, 1,768 people, open label, major heart events through 18 months. Graded A because it is a new trial in people of one of the site's treatments with hard outcomes; it is borderline with B, since it compares two dosing targets rather than testing whether the drug works, and has no result.

items.story: Wang and colleagues, Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice, 2026-11-06: pooled analysis of ten GLP-1 outcome trials (87,334 people), effect over time
items.note: Abstract confirms hazard ratio 0.856 (0.810-0.905). The abstract says early reductions that weaken over time were suggested by the model but were imprecise, and all intervals included 1; it speaks of the regimens modelled, and I could not confirm it singles out semaglutide.

items.story: Baldwin and colleagues, Cardiovascular Research, 2026-11-07: colchicine vs placebo in 111 people with coronary disease, no fall in artery inflammation on scans
items.note: Abstract confirms 111 people (55 vs 56), 24 weeks, main outcome P = 0.38, a white-cell ratio fell (P = 0.033), blood pressure rose less. The C-reactive protein change was only a trend (P = 0.060), so 'a blood marker fell' is true of the white-cell ratio. A randomised result in people, but on a scan measure, so graded B rather than A.

items.story: SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT: survodutide heart-safety trial, Zealand Pharma release, 2026-11-09
items.note: Release confirms 5,530 adults, hazard ratio 0.89 (0.67-1.18) for the five-part outcome, no reduction claimed, Chicago meeting, The Lancet the same day, people with type 2 diabetes included. The release says 5,530 where Healio says 5,508. Registry status of NCT06077864 not checked.

items.story: Circulation meeting abstract 17297, 2026-11-02: what changes the link between protein-based organ age gaps and outcome in 3,194 people with heart failure
items.note: Crossref abstract confirms 3,194 people, four groups, 1,465 events, median 2.0 years, all organ age gaps predicted outcome, differences by diabetes, blood pressure and severity. Crossref's published date is 2026-11-02 (record created 2026-11-06). A meeting abstract, not a full paper.

items.story: Circulation meeting abstract 10037, 2026-11-02: design and starting characteristics of ARTEMIS, ziltivekimab after a heart attack, 8,346 people in 24 countries
items.note: Crossref abstract confirms 8,346 randomised, 24 countries, no results. The registry completion date of 2027-01-29 was not checked. A design abstract.

items.story: Registry NCT07241390 (Eli Lilly, ATTAIN-Outcomes, orforglipron heart-outcomes trial, 7,140 people) updated 2026-11-04
items.note: Confirmed: recruiting, 7,140 people, main completion 2031-08, last update posted 2026-11-04. First posted 2025-11-21, so this is a routine edit; what changed is not shown.

items.story: Novo Nordisk third-quarter 2026 results: write-down on ziltivekimab (trade report by ChemXplore, 2026-11-05, on the 2026-11-04 report)
items.note: The trade report says 1.4 billion US dollars of impairments, 0.7 billion for ziltivekimab, as claimed. This agrees with the company's own filed report (8.7 billion and 4.6 billion Danish kroner). The underlying event is dated 2026-11-04. The grade is for the story; this item adds nothing to S1012.

items.story: Circulation meeting abstract 17152, 2026-11-02: protein-based organ age gaps and outcome in 2,579 people with heart failure, heart age gap hazard ratio 1.36
items.note: Crossref abstract confirms every figure: 2,579 people, two groups (PHFS, WashU), median 2.0 years, 1,254 events, heart age gap 1.36 (1.32-1.40). A sister abstract to S1174 from overlapping groups, but a separate abstract. Meeting abstract, not a full paper.

items.story: United States Food and Drug Administration, 2026-11-09: all GLP-1 drugs must carry a warning about a rare cause of sudden vision loss (NAION)
items.note: Confirmed on the agency's page: twelve listed products including Wegovy, Ozempic, Zepbound, Mounjaro and Foundayo; 126 trials, 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 patient-years; records study showed a raised risk against DPP-4 drugs (hazard ratio 1.43) but not against SGLT-2 drugs (1.19, not significant). A regulator's decision on safety, not on benefit.

items.story: Ohe, Research Square preprint, 2026-11-04: pooled analysis of 162 placebo-controlled trials of GLP-1 drugs and tirzepatide on falls, fractures and lean mass
items.note: Confirmed: serious falls and fractures not increased overall, lean mass 2.76 kg lower than placebo. The claim leaves out a point in the abstract: in the SELECT trial fracture risk rose with age, with hip and pelvis fractures at 75 and over 17 of 703 against 4 of 663. One author, not peer reviewed.

items.story: Registry NCT07783802 (Eli Lilly, clazakizumab in 120 adults with raised inflammation) updated 2026-11-03
items.note: Confirmed: recruiting, started 2026-08-27, 120 people, main measure the percentage change in an inflammation blood marker at week 12, main completion 2027-05, last update posted 2026-11-03. The registry field says phase 2 (the claim says 2b). First posted 2026-08-25, so this is an edit, not a new trial.

items.story: Bao and colleagues, Environmental Research, 2026-11-06: artificial light at night and faster organ ageing on protein clocks in 37,323 UK Biobank participants
items.note: Abstract confirms 37,323 people, eleven organ systems, strongest link for the brain. Uses the clocks as an outcome; does not test disease prediction.

items.story: ZEUS trial of ziltivekimab: BioSpace report, 2026-11-09, on the meeting presentation and the case for testing in less sick patients
items.note: Confirmed. The presentation itself was on 2026-11-07; this report is dated 2026-11-09. The first news that ZEUS missed its goal came in late July 2026, before the window. BioSpace says Novo ended HERMES and ATHENA and that ARTEMIS continues, which agrees with Novo's report (S1012) and not with Healio's line that HERMES is continuing (S1113).

items.story: Baechle, Furman and colleagues, bioRxiv preprint, 2026-11-02: a 30-protein immune 'age' signature (iPACE) tracking heart-disease risk and death in older adults
items.note: Confirmed: thirty proteins, two independent groups, no sizes in the abstract, linked to two kinds of heart disease and death. First published 2026-11-02 though the DOI carries 2026-10-27. Not peer reviewed; one signature, not an age per organ.

items.story: ZEUS trial of ziltivekimab: the NEJM paper itself, Ridker and colleagues, online 2026-11-07
items.note: Crossref confirms title, first author and online date 2026-11-07. I did not open the journal page either; the figures in the claims match the HCPLive and Healio reports I read (see S1120, S1113).
